previous_versions.body: We should make a clear destinction between device bound and synced passkey based authentication. The  former can only be hardware based while the latter can be both. If you read the documents above, you will find several caveats that need to be considered to ensure you are implementing the former (device bound) and not the latter (synced).

We should make a clear destinction between device bound and synced passkey based authentication. The  former can only be hardware based while the latter can be both hardware-based and software-based. If you read the documents above, you will find several caveats that need to be considered to ensure you are implementing the former (device bound) and not the latter (synced).

I’ll reiterate my stand here in case someone finds it later. see original comment: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2970#issuecomment-2855470509

Having requirements for cryptographic is important. WebAuthN and FIDo are just standards and frameworks. You need to apply them correctly in the same way as with OAuth.

Some things to consider:

MFA and hardware-based authentication are additive, not supplementary.
FIDO2/U2F tokens can be software-based and stored in a password manager, but that does not give any high assurance needed for what is being considered above from a risk perspective.
When FIDO2/U2F tokens are backed up, they lose their attestation. For high assurance, believe it or not, backup is not allowed. I know this doesn't seem easy, but the entire population of the European Union seems to do just fine despite it.
So for ASVS L3 authenticators, the following requirement should hold:

1. The authenticator must be device-bound.
2. The authenticator must require multi-factor.
3. The authenticator can not be backed up.
4. The authentication must be performed in an attested and trusted execution environment (TEE) or by authenticators with AAL3 assurance or equivalent.

"or equivalent" is important because each European member nation is implementing their eIDAS LoA3 authenticator that is not necessarily based on FIDO2 or WebAuthN
